newsitem.title: CONGO: Gabon Ebola deaths reach 10, WHO says.
newsitem.headline: Gabon Ebola deaths reach 10, WHO says.

text.p: The death toll from the latest outbreak of Ebola in Gabon has reached 10, the World Health Organisation said from neighbouring Congo on Wednesday.
WHO's Africa headquarters in Brazzaville said in a statement four other Ebola victims were in hospital in northeastern Gabon where the haemorrhagic virus killed 13 people in February.
Gabon confirmed on Tuesday that 14 people had caught the virus in the region since July 24, WHO said.
Ebola has a fatality rate of about 80 percent.
The first victim in the latest outbreak was a hunter who probably caught the virus in the forest and died on August 23 in a hospital at Boue, east of the capital Libreville.
Forty of about 60 people who came into contact with the victims were under observation, WHO added.
At least 13 people died in the area last February in an outbreak of Ebola, which is marked by fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and massive bleeding.
Health officials said then the virus broke out among families who ate or handled dead chimpanzees in the remote area.
Ebola is transmitted by direct contact with blood secretions or body fluids.
The virus struck in Kikwit, Zaire in May 1995, killing 245 people. A single victim in Ivory Coast last December survived.
